# Frozen fictional PDF corpus v1

Task P3-02-FX, frozen 2026-11-19, before financial extraction rules exist. All 13 PDFs (21 pages) are fictional test inputs. They are not examples of authenticated financial statements or evidence of real-layout support.

`manifest.json` contains source annotations and SHA-256 hashes. The Aster reference has all 12 financial fields for two years (24 values), matching `../aster_components.json`. The remaining development PDFs cover grouped numbers, a loss, zero, blank/dash interest, reversed year columns, missing/conflicting units and dates, duplicate/conflicting matches, ambiguous labels, and invalid number tokens. Note-reference digits occur in a separate column.

The second business/layout is reserved for held-out evaluation, with 20 present values and missing interest/current maturities. It changes units, row order, year-column order, and spacing. Integrity checks and visual QA may read it; do not run a financial extractor against it until the first extractor version and development results are frozen. Do not tune using its labels, amounts, or extraction output. Record evaluation runs separately without changing this frozen manifest. Tuning against it requires a replacement holdout for the next unbiased evaluation.

## Annotation conventions

- `pages` order gives the physical 1-based PDF page; each page has one ruled table.
- `headers` is table row 1. `rows` order gives data rows starting at table row 2. Label and note are columns 1 and 2; `values` order gives amount columns starting at column 3.
- Each value records its exact printed token, intended year, parsed decimal amount, exact INR amount, and expected issues. Missing/ambiguous context or values never have a usable normalized INR value. Unmapped labels have `field: null`. Absent rows are absent, never zero.
- Page `unit`/`multiplier` are null for unresolved unit context; `year_start` is null for unresolved period context. Expected issue names describe behaviour to implement, not current extractor output or financial evidence states.
- `annotation_author` and `independent_checker` distinguish agent self-checks from independent review. No independent human or finance-reviewer approval has been obtained.

The annotations were authored from the existing Aster reference and separately specified Birch figures. They were checked against PDF text/table cells, Decimal arithmetic, and rendered pages. These are source-integrity checks, not financial-extraction accuracy measurements.

## Reproduce and verify

From the repository root:

```bash
python backend/tests/build_pdf_corpus.py
cd backend
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_pdf_corpus.py
```

On Windows use `.venv/Scripts/python.exe` for Pytest. The generator uses the shared dependency-free test PDF writer; it requires no new packages and refuses to write a PDF whose bytes differ from its frozen hash. Run it only when intentionally reproducing corpus files. Pytest compares committed bytes to generated bytes without writing anything, verifies exact source cells, checks the 24 reference values and review/split metadata, and passes each development PDF through the bounded upload-inspection worker. Existing pinned pdfplumber performs source-integrity checks; no financial matcher is called.

Keep v1 immutable once extractor tuning begins. Any necessary source/annotation correction needs a documented version change; do not silently regenerate expected results from an extractor. Raw precision/recall, correction effort, public-layout support, and final P5-03 evaluation remain unmeasured.
